paper.title: Generalized Low-Rank Matrix Contextual Bandits with Graph Information

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized low-rank matrix contextual bandit with graph information
unmapped: Actions are rank-one matrices X = p ⊙ q in R^{d1 x d2}; unknown parameter Theta* is a d1 x d2 matrix of rank r; reward mean mu(<X,Theta*>) with canonical exponential-family link
Known undirected similarity graph over actions (Laplacian L) that induces smoothness of expected rewards; graph is side information, not side observations
Learner knows the graph Laplacian, a_mu, and an exploration distribution D satisfying a score-function second-moment bound gamma (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: we can naturally assume that the relationship between the selected action and the reward belongs to the canonical exponential family ... y_t=\mu(\langle X_t,\Theta^*\rangle)+\epsilon_t, where \epsilon_t is the independent sub-Gaussian noise with parameter \omega. ... R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T [\mu(\langle X^*, \Theta^*\rangle) - \mu(\langle X_t, \Theta^*\rangle)]

symbols.k_dim: effective dimension k = (d_1 + d_2 - r) r
symbols.tau: bound on the norm of the residual (redundant) part of the rotated parameter, ||theta*_{k+1:d1d2}|| <= tau

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (score-function second moment bound, ||Theta*||_F<=1, ||X||_F<=1, c_mu <= mu' <= k_mu)
tuning: lambda_perp = c_mu T / (k log(1 + c_mu T / lambda_2))

source.label: the4
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{as1}-\ref{as3}, the regret of Graph-LowGLM-UCB with $\lambda_{\perp}=\frac{c_\mu T}{k \log (1+\frac{c_\mu T}{\lambda_2})}$ is $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \omega k \sqrt{T} +  \tau T\right)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Regret of the second stage only (in the rotated, vectorized space). sigma denotes the paper's sub-Gaussian parameter omega.

symbols.gamma_s: bound on the second moment of the score function of the exploration distribution (Assumption 1)
symbols.c_r: lower bound on the r-th singular value of Theta*

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (score-function second moment <= gamma, ||Theta*||_F<=1, ||X||_F<=1, 0 < c_mu <= mu'(x) <= k_mu for |x|<=1)
conditions of Lemma 1 on the Laplacians (L_h = lambda I and the Kronecker identity)
r-th singular value of Theta* at least c_r > 0
tuning: T_1 >= zeta sqrt(d_1 d_2 gamma r T)/c_r
lambda_perp = c_mu T / (k log(1 + c_mu T/lambda_2))
tau = c_1 zeta^2 d_1 d_2 gamma r log(2(d_1+d_2)/delta)/(T_1 c_r^2)

source.label: the5
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{as1}-\ref{as3}, suppose we run Algorithm \ref{algo1} with $T_1 \geq  \frac{ \zeta \sqrt{d_1 d_2 \gamma r T} }{c_r}$, $\lambda_{\perp}=\frac{c_\mu T}{k \log (1+\frac{c_\mu T}{\lambda_2})}$, $\tau=\frac{c_1 \zeta^2 d_1 d_2 \gamma r \log \left(\frac{2\left(d_1+d_2\right)}{\delta}\right)}{T_1 c_r^2}$, the overall regret is $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} \left(\frac{  \zeta \sqrt{d_1 d_2 \gamma r T} }{c_r} \right)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Tuning of T_1 uses zeta, gamma and c_r (problem quantities) so the learner implicitly knows them. Paper's r is rank r_rank. Derivation is loose (proof is sketchy), recorded as stated.
